title: WHY DOES THE MOON ALWAYS SHOW US THE SAME FACE?
subtitle: A curious story about the rhythm of our closest neighbour

pages.caption: Earth and the Moon are linked by gravity.
pages.text: Have you ever noticed that the Moon seems to show us the same face every night? It is not a coincidence. The Moon rotates on its axis at almost exactly the same rate as it travels around Earth.

pages.caption: Gravity shapes the motion of objects in space.
pages.text: This remarkable pattern is called tidal locking. Over billions of years, Earth’s gravity gradually slowed the Moon’s rotation until the two movements became synchronized.

pages.caption: Sunlight reaches different parts of the Moon.
pages.text: That does not mean the far side of the Moon is always dark. It receives sunlight just like the side we see. The phrase “dark side” is therefore a little misleading.

pages.caption: Space exploration continues to reveal new discoveries.
pages.text: The Moon still has many secrets. Space missions have helped scientists understand its surface, but new discoveries continue to change what we know about our nearest celestial neighbour.

title: WHY DO WE DREAM?
subtitle: A journey into the stories our minds create at night

pages.caption: Sleep is an active time for the brain.
pages.text: Every night, our minds create strange stories while we sleep. Some dreams feel surprisingly real, while others disappear as soon as we wake up. Scientists are still exploring why we dream.

pages.caption: Memories and emotions may influence our dreams.
pages.text: One idea is that dreams help us process memories and emotions. During sleep, the brain organizes information from the day and may connect experiences in unexpected ways.

pages.caption: A new morning often makes a dream harder to remember.
pages.text: We do not remember every dream. Our ability to recall a dream depends partly on when we wake up and how quickly we pay attention to it. Keeping a notebook nearby may help.

title: HOW DO TREES COMMUNICATE?
subtitle: The surprising connections beneath a forest floor

pages.caption: A forest is full of hidden connections.
pages.text: A forest may look quiet, but trees are constantly responding to their surroundings. Through their roots and relationships with fungi, plants can exchange resources and chemical signals.

pages.caption: Fungi can form networks around plant roots.
pages.text: Tiny fungal threads can connect with tree roots. These partnerships help plants absorb nutrients from the soil. Researchers study how resources sometimes move through these underground networks.

pages.caption: There is still much to learn about forest ecosystems.
pages.text: It is tempting to imagine trees talking like people, but the science is more complex. Understanding these connections helps us appreciate how many living things depend on one another.
